entries.english: Judicial proceedings, 1563–1590, in Count Ludwig Casimir von Hohenlohe-Neuenstein’s case against Sebastian and Hans von Crailsheim and their associates over hunting rights around Kirchberg. The file concerns hunts by the von Crailsheim family at Crippelberg and a hare net seized from them by Hohenlohe. At Hornberg, Crailsheim arrested two Kirchberg citizens; after an Imperial Chamber Court mandate they were released, Crailsheim was charged the resulting court costs, ordered to refrain from future seizures, and required to provide surety. Both sides were permitted formally to submit evidence and pleadings about the hunts and net. The records include the original protest by the von Rosenberg as captain of the knights against the confiscation; Hohenlohe’s response and petitions; the mandate and its service; reports and pleadings; witness questions and examination instructions; the Crailsheim submissions and objections; and agreements concerning the stream and millrace above Horn Mill, the fishing water called the Old Castle, sale of Hornberg-vogt properties in the Kirchberg district, boundary stones and communal rights, division of Hornberg and Märklingen, grazing rights on Sulzberg, the small lake at Beuhel, livestock damage penalties, and other disputes over subjects’ properties (1560). Other enclosures include the castle peace agreement between Count Palatine Otto and Adam von Hundt concerning jointly held Hornberg Castle, judgments concerning two detained subjects, Crailsheim’s surety, objections to the sufficiency of sureties, and cost schedules. The file contains items 1–94 and measures 6 cm.
